rationale:
Final iteration, so this candidate is both the last development race and the design that will face the unseen final track. I am keeping the iteration-10 design unchanged because it is the best evidence available (score 700.19, the best so far). It finishes 20/20 on oval (1.97 s) and 20/20 on s-bend (2.32 s), with max_error 0.0096 and 0.0205. Slalom still never finishes (0/20, progress 0.53, 1.35 line-loss events per run, off track in every run).

Why no change: the last several single-variable steps moved the score by only about 3 points (iteration 9 to 10: +3.0), and each gain was paid for by a small rise in line losses on slalom. Iteration 7 (kp 5.0) and iteration 8 (16 mm sensors, +/-4 cm) both lost s-bend finishes and scored lower. Any untested change now carries real risk of losing the 20/20 completions on oval and s-bend, which are worth far more than the slalom progress gained. Because no iteration follows this one, a regression could not be corrected, so the safe choice is the validated design.

Expected result: about the same as iteration 10 on the development tracks (about 700), with oval and s-bend completing. Slalom probably stays at 0 completions. Hypotheses: (a) the final unseen track will behave like oval and s-bend more than slalom, so completion there is likely; (b) the slalom loss is driven by line loss at the sharp alternations, and it would need a sensing or gain change that I cannot validate in this iteration. Measurements wanted from the race: completion and completion_time for each track, progress, max_error and line_loss_events on slalom (location of the loss), and steering_oscillation on s-bend.
